metadata.case_name: CHAN CHUN FAT v. FORTRESS GLORY ENGINEERING LTD

plaintiff.occupation_after: decorative casual worker; construction worker; rigger
plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: car park attendant or petrol station attendant

injuries.description: injury to his left knee (soft tissue injury)
source: A corner of the Trolley hit him in the left knee and he therefore suffered injuries to his back.

Dr Tio opined that P suffered from an injury to his left knee and back as a result of the Accident, and that the mechanism of injury he sustained was compatible with the diagnoses (i.e. soft tissue injury).
injuries.icd_description: Injury of unspecified muscle, fascia, tendon or bursa at lower leg level

injuries.description: injury to his back / lower back (soft tissue injury)
source: A corner of the Trolley hit him in the left knee and he therefore suffered injuries to his back.

Dr Tio opined that P suffered from an injury to his left knee and back as a result of the Accident, and that the mechanism of injury he sustained was compatible with the diagnoses (i.e. soft tissue injury).
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle, fascia or tendon of lower back

manifestations.description: Residual lower back pain rated by P at the scale of 8/10. The pain is aggravated by walking and standing for over half an hour, days of poor weather, lifting a weight of up to 5 kg and bending forward. Stiffness of his lower back.
Residual left knee is intermittent and is aggravated by walking 20 – 30 flights of stairs and kneeling for over 2 -3 minutes.
Residual left knee clicks brought about by staircase walking especially when going up.
Puncture wound found over the left knee skin surface.
Tenderness over the low back with decreased range of movement of the spine due to pain.
Unable to carry heavy weights of more than 5 kg.

treatments_received: Accident and Emergency treatment at United Christian Hospital (attended same day and discharged the same day)

losses.description: Loss of earning capacity award HK$50,000 (2% permanent loss of earning capacity as opined by Dr Tio)
